$comment: The source of sf-icon-button's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/icon-button (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

button-attributes.summary: Attributes an external project template may put on its button; the built-in template does not read them

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

x-summary: Native icon-only action with token geometry, accessible naming and shared loading semantics.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-icon-button for a compact action that is unambiguous from one familiar icon and has a concise accessible name.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not omit aria-label when no visible text names the action
Do not use the large-surface radius as a normal control variation
Do not keep a loading action enabled

x-decisions: a11y-role: button, the native <button> the template draws (the host is display:contents). The name is the host's aria-label, passed to the native button with the badge phrase after it (§3.1, §4.8); an icon-only control has no other text.

key-effects: Tab reach. Enter and Space are the native button's own activation, not an effect of the closed list; the native click bubbles as before. No press event: the parts catalogue gives sf-icon-button none, and sf-button's press is the target the stands wrote for sf-button alone.

setter: setButtonAttributes is not an action (§4.4): button-attributes is a writable object setting (a property), and the method stays a helper that writes it; it no longer writes the object into an attribute.

legacy names: type -> appearance, variant -> kind and tightness -> spacing leave the settings and are dated setting aliases (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01); tightness's words are spacing's value aliases (low/high/highest -> compact/comfortable/spacious). ghost stays an appearance of its own here: the class sf-icon-button--ghost draws it.
badge-cap is a number with min 1; badge-count stays a string capped by badge-cap.
aria-label is a host attribute, never a setting (§3.1); the template reads it from the host.

template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift). The host stays display:contents: geometry lives on > button.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (add, default primary) plus tonal and outline, the close kind, the error status, a count badge, loading, disabled and segments.
css-variables: the seven public variables of src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json the class sheet already reads (§6).

folder: icon-buttons takes the tag's name, icon-button (§3, §21, §16 item 16); the loader bundle is cl-icon-button, cl-icon-buttons stays a forwarding rule and smart/icon-buttons/js/icon-buttons.js a forwarding script (css/icon-buttons.css its sheet) until 2026-12-01 (change journal path-smart-icon-buttons-to-icon-button). The registry id stays smart.icon-buttons.
version 1.1.0: renamed members behind dated aliases are a minor (§4.10, §16.20).
